profiles.name: Douglas Musekiwa
profiles.source: Douglas Musekiwa biography from Hatfield Art Community, owner-supplied 20 November 2026
profiles.introduction: Douglas Musekiwa is a Zimbabwean stone sculptor from Guruve whose work developed through an apprenticeship and exploration of abstract form.
profiles.biography:
Douglas Musekiwa was born in 1986 in Zimbabwe's Guruve District, a region known for its stone-carving tradition. He completed his primary and secondary education there and grew up in a large family. At the age of twenty, he joined the sculpting studio of his cousin, Eckel Nyamhondoro. During four years of training and practical experience, Musekiwa found an enduring commitment to sculpture and decided to devote his working life to art.

He later joined Stindi Art Gallery, where he worked alongside the Sango art family, Tendai Rukodzi and other sculptors. This environment encouraged him to experiment and develop an abstract style of his own. He began working as a full-time artist and sold pieces both locally and internationally, according to his supplied biography.

Today, Musekiwa works with a group of artists at Hatfield Art Community, along Airport Road in Hatfield, Harare. His sculpture Coil, represented in the House of Mabwe collection, offers an example of how a recognisable bird form can be carried into abstraction. A turning spiral transforms the bird's familiar outline into a continuous, rhythmic shape, bringing a sense of movement to the solidity of stone.
